behavior: InvoiceReceiverFactory and InvoiceReceiver v1 implement every rule in packages/contracts/AGENTS.md, proven by unit, fuzz, invariant, cross-chain, fork and Halmos symbolic tests
acceptance: packages/contracts/src has InvoiceTypes.sol, InvoiceReceiverFactory.sol and InvoiceReceiver.sol implementing the Terms, Factory and Receiver rules of packages/contracts/AGENTS.md

forge test passes: a unit test per rule, fuzz tests on amounts and time, five invariants (exact settlement, conservation, executor never paid, owed amount kept before settleDeadline, invoice token never recovered), the cross-chain CREATE2 test, and the Base Sepolia fork test with real USDC (CI uses the public RPC)
Halmos check_settle, check_refund and check_recoverNeverTakesInvoiceToken pass locally and in CI
Breaking a rule makes the tests fail: removing the owed-amount guard in refundable() and removing the settle caller check each fail forge tests, and the first also fails Halmos
notes: 2026-10-08 review pass by reviewer: No money or security issue found. forge test: 45 pass, 1 skipped (fork without RPC); fork test with real Base Sepolia USDC passes; Halmos 0.3.3: check_settle, check_refund, check_recoverNeverTakesInvoiceToken pass. Mutations checked in a scratch copy: removing the owed guard in refundable() fails 4 forge tests (unit, fuzz, invariant) and Halmos check_refund; removing the settle caller check fails 3 unit tests and Halmos check_settle. Invariant handler measured: settle succeeds in 184/257 runs, refund in 202 (195 after deadline), so invariants are not vacuous. Checked: executor can only pay recipient; refunds keep amount until settleDeadline (boundary <= / > consistent with settle); recover blocks invoice token by address and by balance-drop check (Arc native/USDC; only sub-1e12-wei dust above the 6-dec balance could leave, which is not owed money); CEI + nonReentrant; implementation reverts NotClone; predict/deploy share _address so validation and address match; salt = keccak(args); factory address commits to (authority, executor) via CREATE2 deployer; SafeERC20 covers no-return and false-return tokens; fee-on-transfer reverts RecipientMismatch. Non-blocking notes (tests missing for rules that hold in code, confirmed by throwaway PoCs): no test for nonReentrant on refund/recover; no USDT no-return-value mock (FeeToken stands in); no test that events are emitted; recipient == receiver rejection cannot be tested (hash fixed point); recover's to-address checks untested. invariant_invoiceTokenNeverRecovered is weak (attacker balance <= totalRefunded), but no recover of the invoice token succeeded in any run.

2026-10-08 review pass by reviewer: Re-review after 9f536d9 (tests only; no src changes, confirmed with git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- packages/contracts/src). forge fmt --check and forge test: 50 passed, 1 skipped (fork test without RPC). The new tests are meaningful, checked by mutation in a scratch copy: removing nonReentrant from refund fails test_refundReentrancyBlocked; removing it from recover fails test_recoverReentrancyBlocked; removing recover's to-address check fails test_recoverRejectsBadDestination. NoReturnToken settle+refund passes through SafeERC20; the events test asserts emitter and args for ReceiverDeployed, Settled, Refunded, Recovered. Note: the reentrant call comes from the token, so without the guard it would still fail on Unauthorized; the tests catch the guard's removal through the error selector, which is the most a test can show here, since only the refund authority can call. Earlier findings stand: no money or security issue; Halmos and the fork test passed in the first review, and this commit changes neither.
